original_plan.hypothesis: Phase A's execution gap is closed only for the training half: the direct RL run reached real PPO sampling and optimization (8 complete rollouts, 64 optimizer steps, checkpoint published), whereas the previously recorded attempt never sampled. The independent evaluation half remains unclosed: the single evaluation episode produced no metrics because the evaluate subprocess aborted with a NameError (json not defined) in tools/rl/checks.py after the rollout reported a NaN/Inf QVEL instability at t = 0.2205 s. original_plan.interpretation: New results this phase. (1) The historical training blocker is retired: the run inherited unchanged weights (policy_sha256 cd6a23b8…, num_timesteps 0) and exited with policy_sha256 08625aba…, num_timesteps 1024, 32 optimization epochs across 8 rollout optimizations and 64 optimizer steps, so at least two complete PPO batches executed and a current checkpoint (step-00001024-5c37317d) plus a previous one were published; parameter_change_l2 2.1804 shows the frozen configuration did produce updates. (2) The evaluation requirement is still unmet: the one permitted episode was dispatched, charged, and its artifact records passed false with episodes [], counts null, evaluation_elapsed_s null and no checkpoint/policy identity, with consumption_uncertain true and the scope note that the episode charge is retained and no zero-cost claim is made. (3) The run status additionally reports failure_stage 'checkpoint publication' although a current and previous checkpoint exist, so the published-artifact set and the metric set are not jointly sufficient to freeze a solution. Consequences: task_performance is unmeasured; no selected_execution can be confirmed (the recorded eligibility reasons remain 'result did not pass complete original task evaluation', 'exact evaluated checkpoint identity missing', 'declared confirmations already recorded'); interface acceptance is evidenced only up to the crash point; improvement attribution stays withheld; and a single nominal episode would support no robustness claim even if it had completed. Budget reality: training_runs 1/1, training_actions 1024/1024 and evaluation_episodes 1/1 are consumed, diagnostic_physics_steps and replays are 0, and backend_solves is 1/1, so no further RL action is permitted in this phase and no ceiling may be raised. The two observations — a harness import defect on the metrics path and a rollout instability warning at t = 0.2205 s — are reported as facts only; I make no root-cause or algorithm-superiority claim, and I do not treat any relaxed or merely mathematically feasible formulation as evidence about original MuJoCo task acceptance. Because a missing evaluation does not close the execution gap while a complete task failure would, the evidence-based next step is diagnosis of the evaluation pathway (and of whether the instability is a property of the frozen candidate/policy integration) under a newly authorized allocation, since repairing the metrics path in tools/rl/checks.py and re-evaluating both exceed the ceilings of the current allocation.
original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop after exactly one direct training run, one terminal status query, one evaluation attempt of the saved checkpoint and one explicit immutable-evidence read, as scoped by Phase A. No retraining, no second evaluation, no diagnostics, no replays, no resume and no raised ceilings; the failed evaluation is retained and its charge is not disputed.
original_plan.weakening_observation: This reading is wrong if the evaluation artifact actually contained recorded episode metrics (a position_error inside the 0.01 m tolerance) or a matching checkpoint/policy hash, which would make 'evaluation missing' false and would supply a development result to confirm. Equally, if the terminal status had shown zero attempted actions or a failure before sampling, the claim that the Phase A execution gap is closed would not hold; and if active_seconds had exceeded the 90 s allocation or the effective PPO settings differed from the frozen ones, the frozen-configuration claim would fail.
